subject: geography
chapter_title: Use of Computer in Data Processing and Mapping

concepts.title: Computer System: Hardware and Software
concepts.definition: A computer system combines hardware - the physical units of input, central processing, memory and output - with software, the programmes that instruct it; system software manages the machine while application software such as databases and spreadsheets does the user's work.
concepts.key_idea: Input, processing, storage and output form the data cycle every computer runs, whether desktop or server.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy304.txt hardware components and software types sections

solution_steps.explain: hardware is physical machinery, software is its instructions

primary memory works instantly, secondary memory stores permanently

concepts.title: Databases for Geographic Data
concepts.definition: A database management system stores geographic data as organised tables of records and fields that can be sorted, queried and joined; attributes of villages, districts or weather stations sit in rows that software can filter and summarise instantly.
concepts.key_idea: Structured tables turn repetitive clerical work - sorting, totalling, searching - into single commands.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy304.txt database structure and query discussion

solution_steps.explain: rows hold records for each village or district, columns hold fields like literacy
a query selects records meeting a condition, such as density above a threshold
joining attribute tables to map units powers thematic mapping

concepts.title: Computer-Assisted Computation
concepts.definition: Spreadsheet-style software computes means, totals and ratios over entire columns at once; entering village populations and areas, the computer evaluates the density for every row and even averages the results, replacing hours of manual arithmetic.
concepts.key_idea: The computer evaluates average density as the sum of all row densities divided by the number of rows.

solution_steps.explain: the software totals the density column
the average over all rows gives the overall density

concepts.title: Computer Mapping and Its Advantages
concepts.definition: Computer mapping converts attribute tables into thematic maps automatically - choropleth shades, dot patterns and symbols drawn to scale - allowing quick redesign of classes, colours and layouts, which manual cartography achieved only through slow redrafting.
concepts.key_idea: Digital maps are editable arguments: change the classification and the same data argues differently, in minutes.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy304.txt computer mapping capabilities and advantages sections

solution_steps.explain: attribute tables link to area units for shading
